whisper_segs.text: Good morning, it's seven o'clock on Monday, the 23rd of February. This is Morning Ireland
with Audrey Carville and Sarah McInerney.
Good morning. Coming up between now and nine, four years of war, no sign of an end. The
bombs continue to fall on Ukraine. Also this morning, online fraud on the rise. Flares
in Dundalk, Mar-a-Lago killing what Ireland is reading and Buckley's BAFTA.
In business, renewed tariff uncertainty pushes gold up as the dollar dips and hotel industry
says mounting costs pose a major challenge.
And coming up in sport, 18-year-old debutant Kobe McDonald lights up Clonis and Rory McIlroy
just edged out at the Genesis Invitational.
We're here with you until nine o'clock here on RT Radio 1 and the RT News Channel. The
news is read now by Susan Jackson.
Garthi have said there's been a significant increase in reported and suspected fraud offences,
particularly online fraud, which rose by over 130% last year. Provisional Gartha crime figures
also show reductions in most other serious crime categories, including robberies, thefts
and sex offences. More than 200 people were arrested and 250 criminal charges were preferred
every day in 2025. The figures form the basis of official crime figures from the Central
Statistics Office, which are expected to be published next month. Our crime correspondent
Paul Reynolds.
These Gartha figures illustrate the changing nature of crime, with more of it being committed
online. There have been significant increases in online deception, card shopping and accommodation
frauds, money laundering and forgery. Overall, fraud offences were up 137% last year, but
Garthi say this can partly be explained by the requirement for financial institutions
to report all cases of fraud or suspected fraud. In cybercrime, there was a 27% increase
in harmful communications, such as the distribution of grossly offensive communications and in
people recording and distributing intimate images. There were significant reductions
in thefts, robberies and burglaries. Rape and other sexual offences dropped by 12%.
On gangland crime, drug dealing offences were up 13%, but cases of drugs for personal use
dropped by 6%, an indication, Garthi say, of their focus on suppliers as opposed to
users. Shootings were down 3%. There were no gangland murders last year. Garthi also
say that last year they arrested more than 200 people, issued over 500 summonses and
preferred over 250 criminal charges every day. The three people who died following a
three-vehicle collision in County Oma on Saturday night have been named locally. Four other
people were injured in the crash, which occurred on the Moy Road near Armagh City. A total
of seven people were killed on Irish roads over the weekend. Our northern correspondent,
Conor McCauley. The three victims were from the counties of Tyrone and Armagh. 31-year-old
father of four, Connor Quinn, died in the crash on the main road between Dungannon and
Armagh City. He was from near Coal Island. 23-year-old mother of one, Laura Hoy, from
Cookstown, and 49-year-old John Guy, who had six children and lived in Cady, were also
killed. The collision involved three cars. Police said the emergency services had been
met with an extremely difficult scene with multiple casualties. They had arrived within
12 minutes of the accident and had done what they could to help. Three other people were
taken to hospital for treatment. Police said they were in a stable condition. The accident
has shocked the communities from which the victims came. Politicians said people were
reeling and families had been plunged into mourning. Conor McCauley, RT News, Belfast.
Jessie Buckley has become the first Irish woman to win the leading actress category
at the annual BAFTA ceremony for her performance in Hamnet. The film, adapted from the book
by author Maggie O'Farrell, was also named Outstanding British Film of the Year. Our
Arts and Media correspondent, Evelyn O'Rourke, was at the award ceremony. Last night, Jessie
Buckley became the first Irish woman to win the leading actress category at the annual
BAFTA ceremony. One of the final awards to be presented on the night, her win was announced
by her fellow Irish actor Cillian Murphy. While there was disappointment for her co-star
Paul Meskell, who'd been nominated in the Best Supporting Actor category, he lost out
to Sean Penn, who won for his role in one battle after another. The Hamlet team also
took home the award for Outstanding British Film. There were more surprises too on the
night as actor Richard Arameo first won the Rising Star Award for his role in the movie
I Swear, and then a short while later, beat off competition from Leonardo DiCaprio and
Timothee Chalamet, amongst others, to secure the Leading Actor Award. There was continued
award success too for Dubliner Richie Bainham, who was part of the team who won the BAFTA
Special Visual Effects Award for their work on Avatar, Fire and Ash. More success too
for the Dublin-based Element Pictures co-produced film, My Father's Shadow, which was named
Outstanding Debut by a British writer, director or producer. Next stop for Jessie Buckley
and Hamlet though is the Oscars, taking place in Los Angeles in just a few weeks' time.
